caveats.text: Lucent revenue basis: $8.1B total customer financing commitments (verified, FY2002 10-K) over FY2000 revenue of $28.904B as restated in that same 10-K (continuing-operations basis, verified) is about 28%. On revenue as originally reported in the FY2000 10-K405 ($33.813B, verified) the same ratio is about 24%. The page must name one basis; the default is the restated 28% and must be labelled as such.

Lucent FY2000 loan commitments ($6.7B), advances ($1.3B), guarantees ($1.4B) and the Verizon (13%) and AT&T (10%) customer shares are in the FY2000 10-K405. The FY1999 comparatives ($7.1B, $1.6B) are carried from the same filing but have not been checked line by line. Totals for later years are in the FY2002 10-K: $8.1B (FY2000), $5.3B (FY2001), $1.3B (FY2002).

Winstar ($2B committed, ~$700M write-off) and the SEC revenue-recognition matter ($1.148B revenue, $25M fine) are from a secondary source (Tunguz) and unverified. The SEC matter is specific to Lucent in 2000 and is not an allegation about any AI-era company.
Nortel drawn customer financing at 31 Dec 2000 is unverified ($1.08B net per press citing the SEC filing vs $1.6B per another outlet). Undrawn commitments of about $4.1B are verified.

The Lucent/Nortel parallel is a framing used by commentators, not a tested conclusion. Differences: Nvidia generates tens of billions in quarterly free cash flow; buyers are among the richest companies; GPU useful life is disputed vs decades-long fiber life; Nvidia says no payments have been made under its guarantees.
Lucent's customer defaults came in 2001, about a year after peak financing (Winstar Chapter 11 on April 18, 2001). No confirmed public default on a GPU-backed loan had been found as of October 2026.

bull_arguments.claim: Nvidia's exposure is conditional and small relative to cash generation: guarantees are a ceiling tied to residual value, undrawn, and Nvidia has paid nothing; Q3 net income was $65.3B and FCF is large. Lucent financed customers from a far weaker cash position.
bull_arguments.who: Nvidia disclosures and analysts such as UBS (exposure up to ~13% of 2026E revenue); Data Center Knowledge on guarantee structure

bull_arguments.claim: Demand is real and backlogged: Nvidia revenue +103% y/y with Rubin shipping; CoreWeave backlog ~$132.5B with 2026 guidance raised; interim CEO Kress says hyperscalers are looking for more compute; H100 rental rates rising (Huang, Sept).
bull_arguments.who: Nvidia (Colette Kress); CoreWeave management; Jensen Huang (Sept 2026)

bull_arguments.claim: Buyers are the richest firms on earth with operating cash flow, unlike dot-com startups; policymakers expect build-out to continue (NEC's Kevin Hassett); a 25-50 bp tightening alone would not end the build-out.
bull_arguments.who: Kevin Hassett (NEC); sell-side commentary summarized by Yahoo Finance

bull_arguments.claim: Rating and credit stress shows up in a small set of levered names; Nvidia's CDS (~139 bp) is far below Oracle's and CoreWeave's, and no public GPU-loan default has occurred.
bull_arguments.who: CNBC/Deutsche Bank spread data; AM Compute tracker

bull_arguments.claim: Jensen Huang's public stance: 'circular financing' fears are overstated ('If that is, let's do more of that').

Hyperscaler spending is funded largely by operating cash flow and is still guided up: Microsoft reported $58.0B of operating cash flow against $39.4B of capital additions in its latest quarter, and Meta's 2026 capex outlook midpoint is about $140B.
bull_arguments.who: Microsoft 10-Q and Meta Q3 2026 results (company filings)

bear_arguments.claim: Circular flows inflate reported demand: Nvidia funds or backstops customers (OpenAI guarantee up to $105B, equity stakes, unsold-capacity purchase commitments) who buy its chips, and the guarantee depends on an OpenAI lacking investment-grade credit.
Neoclouds depend on Nvidia as 'the bank'; if that support fades many would lose access to capital.
Fed staff: off-balance-sheet leasing and circular financing could amplify losses if AI returns disappoint; AI debt grew fast through opaque structures.
The AI capex race will end when credit is withdrawn; hyperscaler FCF has turned negative and debt issuance is surging ($296B in 2026, $440B plus $300B projected).

GPU useful lives are overstated in depreciation schedules (Burry estimate ~$176B understated depreciation 2026-2028), so collateral is shorter-lived than long-haul fiber was. Chanos questioned why chip owners do not rent chips out themselves.
The Lucent/Nortel parallel: vendor lent to or guaranteed customers who later failed; concentrated customers and rising contingent commitments are the bear framing (framing, not a tested conclusion).
bear_arguments.who: Commentators such as Tomasz Tunguz; Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon on circular concerns

open_questions: We couldn't confirm why Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia's 8-K gives no reason, and only the facts in the filing are used here.
The $9.5B of 'power and systems' guarantees in Nvidia's CFO commentary has no further description, so we can't say who they protect.
We have not checked Nortel's drawn customer financing at the end of 2000 against the filing; reports range from $1.08B to $1.6B.
Lucent and Nortel don't disclose how much revenue came from CLECs and startups in the filings available to us.
Telecom totals for capex and debt depend on how each source defines them.
Oracle's credit-default-swap record varies by data provider (about 151, 288 and 300 bp in different reports), so we show the peak as reported and do not compare it with other dates.
CoreWeave's note maturity (2031 or 2032) and coupon (9.75% or 9.625%) differ between news stories and we have not checked the indenture.
Nvidia's drop from its October high is reported as 36% or 39%, and the exact peak is not confirmed.
Reports that banks struggled to place about $38B of Oracle-linked data-center debt come from one outlet, so treat them as unconfirmed.
Hyperscaler capex figures here come from summaries of the Q3 reports, not from the filings themselves.
The September Fed rate path comes from news coverage; the Fed's own pages are the place to check it.
huang_note: On Nov 12 Nvidia filed an 8-K saying Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO, president and director, and that CFO Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. The filing gave no reason. We don't know the reason and we won't guess.
